note: Senegal, read on 2026-10-30 on the Ministry of the Interior and Public Security's own page on the foreigner's identity card (interieur.gouv.sn, 'Services aux usagers', 'Carte d'identité d'étranger'; the page carries no date). The card is one card for every foreigner, whatever the purpose: the list of documents asks a work contract and, for students, an enrolment certificate and proof of support, so it is written as a general route. Its fee is the fiscal stamp of 15,000 F CFA the list asks for, which is written; the list also asks the receipt of a repatriation deposit whose amount 'varies by country', which isn't a fee and isn't held. The application is lodged with the Division des Polices des Étrangers (DPETV), the national police's foreigners' division, and decided by the Minister after the Directorate-General of the National Police gives its opinion on a first application, so where it is applied for is read as in the country (a reading: the page names the office, not the country). The page says nothing of how long the card lasts or a decision takes, what work it allows, or permanent residence; it names a renewal only as a step in the card's production ('Saisie duplicata ou Renouvellement'), which isn't written as renewable. Read with the Ministry's list of services (the same site), which links the page.
